title: Oregon School Shooting: Former Student Kills Three Children and Teacher in Bend
excerpt: Police identified 16-year-old Griffin J. John II as the shooter at Silver Rail Elementary School, where a teacher who fought the gunman and a parent who shot him were credited with preventing more deaths.
body:
• A 16-year-old former student killed three children aged 5, 8 and 11 and teacher Megan Lambert, 25, at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday afternoon.
  • Police identified the shooter on Friday as Griffin J. John II; a 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher were wounded, and the shooter was killed inside the school by a parent who intervened.
  • Investigators say the motive remains unknown, parents are cooperating, and officers seized computers and electronic devices from the family home under a search warrant.
  • All Bend district schools were closed Friday; families should follow Bend Police and Bend-La Pine Schools updates for reunification, counselling and reopening information.

A former student opened fire inside an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday, killing three young children and a teacher in a special-needs classroom before he was shot dead by a parent who had followed him into the building, police said on Friday. The attack at Silver Rail Elementary School, which began just before 1 p.m. local time, is the latest school shooting to devastate a small American community and reopen national arguments over school security and access to firearms.

Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz identified the shooter at a Friday briefing as Griffin J. John II, 16, a former pupil at the school. Police said he approached on foot, threw a shotgun over a fence and climbed over it, fired at a passing pickup truck, then shot through locked glass doors to get inside. Officers arrived about three minutes after the first 911 call and found the shooter already dead, according to accounts reported by the New York Post and The Times.

What police say happened inside the classroom

Investigators said the shooter entered a special-needs classroom and fired about 15 rounds from a 12-gauge pump-action shotgun. He had roughly 44 remaining rounds on him or in a backpack, and police recovered three types of ammunition. Three children, aged 5, 8 and 11, and their teacher were killed in that room. Another child, aged 7, and a second teacher, aged 54, were taken to hospital with serious injuries.

Inside the room, a teacher confronted the gunman directly. Police said she threw a cellphone at him, tackled him and fought for the shotgun. While they wrestled, a 36-year-old father whose children attend the school entered and shot the gunman. Krantz credited both adults with preventing further deaths, describing the intervention as an act of courage under extreme pressure. The father has been identified in reporting as Kaylub Giamanco, a carpenter who was passing the school after lunch when he heard gunfire.

"everyone wants to know — including us"

— Mike Krantz, Bend Police Chief, on the motive

Victims, families and a community in mourning

The youngest child killed was identified as 5-year-old Rhoam Summer, who had recently started kindergarten. The teacher killed was Megan Lambert, 25, described by her family as a teacher who loved Silver Rail and worked with special-needs pupils. The names of the other two children killed had not been released in the reports reviewed for this article, pending family notification.

On Friday, families gathered at a makeshift memorial outside the school, leaving flowers and balloons, while parents were reunited with children at a local church on Thursday. It was supposed to have been picture day at Silver Rail, a school with about 459 pupils last year. District schools and nearby college campuses were closed on Friday as the investigation continued and counselling was arranged.

Investigation and what remains unknown

Police said the shooter's parents are cooperating and that officers executed a search warrant at the family home, taking computers and other electronic devices to look for clues about planning or motive. Reporting noted the shooter had previously been a special-needs student at the school, a detail the superintendent also referenced on Friday. His mother apologised to reporters on Friday and said she would have prevented the attack if she could have.

Authorities have not announced a motive, and investigators cautioned that searches of devices and interviews will take time. The FBI is assisting local police, according to district reporting. For Indian-American and other immigrant families in the United States, school shootings remain a recurring source of anxiety when choosing schools and neighbourhoods, even though police have given no indication of any targeted ethnic or religious motive in Bend.

What happens next

Police are expected to release further verified details as families are notified and the wounded patients' conditions are updated. Parents in the Bend-La Pine district should monitor official school and police channels rather than social media for reopening dates, counselling locations and any public vigil information. Nationally, the shooting is likely to renew debate in Oregon and in Congress, but no new legislation had been announced in the immediate aftermath covered by these reports.
